questions.hint: Add 125 and 375 first. They make a round number.

questions.prompt: Theo's pumpkin weighs 3 pounds 4 ounces. How many ounces does it weigh? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.hint: Change the 3 pounds into ounces first.
questions.solution: 3 pounds = 3 × 16 = 48 ounces. 48 + 4 = 52 ounces.

questions.prompt: A rectangular garden is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. What is the perimeter of the garden?
questions.hint: Perimeter is the distance all the way around: two lengths and two widths.

questions.prompt:
What number comes next in this pattern?
3, 7, 11, 15, 19, ___
questions.hint: How much is added each time?
questions.solution: The pattern adds 4 each time. 19 + 4 = 23.

questions.prompt: Today is Monday. What day of the week will it be 10 days from today?
questions.hint: In 7 days it will be Monday again.
questions.solution: 7 days from Monday is Monday again. 3 more days: Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday.

questions.prompt: Leo has 3 quarters, 4 dimes and 6 nickels. He buys a juice box for 95¢. How many cents does he have left?
questions.hint: Find how many cents Leo has in all before he buys anything.

questions.prompt: Two apple pies and one cake cost $26 in all. The cake costs $8. How much does one apple pie cost?
questions.hint: Take away the cake's price. What do the two pies cost together?
questions.solution: Two pies cost 26 − 8 = $18. One pie costs 18 ÷ 2 = $9.

questions.prompt: A movie started at 1:50 PM and lasted 1 hour 45 minutes. At what time did the movie end?
questions.hint: Add the 1 hour first, then the 45 minutes.
questions.solution: 1:50 PM + 1 hour = 2:50 PM. 2:50 PM + 10 minutes = 3:00 PM, and 35 more minutes makes 3:35 PM.

questions.prompt: How many 2-digit numbers have digits that add up to 5?
questions.hint: Start with a tens digit of 1 and list them in order.
questions.solution: 14, 23, 32, 41, 50. That is 5 numbers. (05 is not a 2-digit number.)

questions.prompt: What is the largest 3-digit number that can be divided by 8 with no remainder?
questions.hint: Divide 999 by 8. What is the remainder?
questions.solution: 999 ÷ 8 = 124 remainder 7. So 999 − 7 = 992 = 8 × 124 is the largest.

questions.prompt: How many squares of any size are in this 3 by 3 grid?
questions.hint: Count the small 1 by 1 squares, then the 2 by 2 squares, then the 3 by 3 square.
questions.solution: 1 by 1 squares: 9. 2 by 2 squares: 4. 3 by 3 squares: 1. Total: 9 + 4 + 1 = 14.

questions.prompt: In this number pyramid, each box is the sum of the two boxes right below it. What number goes in the top box?
questions.hint: Fill in the pyramid one row at a time, starting from the bottom.
questions.solution: Second row from the bottom: 3 + 5 = 8, 5 + 2 = 7, 2 + 6 = 8. Next row: 8 + 7 = 15, 7 + 8 = 15. Top: 15 + 15 = 30.

questions.prompt: Ana, Ben, Cara and Dev sit in a row of 4 seats. Ana must sit in the first seat. In how many different ways can the four of them sit?
questions.hint: Ana's seat is fixed. How many ways can the other 3 kids fill the other 3 seats?
questions.solution: Seat 2 has 3 choices, seat 3 then has 2 choices, and seat 4 has 1 choice. 3 × 2 × 1 = 6 ways.

questions.prompt: I am a 2-digit number. I am a multiple of 7. My ones digit is 2 more than my tens digit. What number am I?
questions.hint: List the 2-digit multiples of 7: 14, 21, 28, ...
questions.solution: Check the multiples of 7: 14, 21, 28, 35, ... In 35, the ones digit 5 is 2 more than the tens digit 3. No other multiple of 7 works, so the answer is 35.

questions.prompt: Ethan and Zara picked 48 apples altogether. Ethan picked 3 times as many apples as Zara. How many apples did Ethan pick?
questions.hint: If Zara's apples are 1 part, Ethan's are 3 parts. How many parts in all?
questions.solution: Zara has 1 part and Ethan has 3 parts, so 4 parts = 48 apples. 1 part = 48 ÷ 4 = 12. Ethan picked 3 × 12 = 36 apples.

questions.prompt: All corners of this shape are right angles. What is its area?
questions.hint: Think of a full 8 by 6 rectangle with a small corner cut out.
questions.solution: The full rectangle would be 8 × 6 = 48 sq cm. The missing corner is 3 × 2 = 6 sq cm. 48 − 6 = 42 sq cm.

questions.prompt: A bag has 6 red, 5 green and 4 yellow candies. Without looking, what is the fewest number of candies you must take out to be sure you have 3 candies of the same color?
questions.hint: Imagine the unluckiest picks: how many can you take without getting 3 of one color?
questions.solution: Unluckiest case: 2 red, 2 green and 2 yellow, which is 6 candies with no 3 of a color. The 7th candy must make 3 of some color. Answer: 7.

questions.prompt: Use each of the digits 2, 4, 6 and 8 exactly once to make two 2-digit numbers. What is the smallest possible difference between the two numbers?
questions.hint: Make the tens digits close together. Then make the bigger number's ones digit small and the smaller number's ones digit big.
questions.solution: Try tens digits 4 and 6: the bigger number should be as small as possible (62) and the smaller number as big as possible (48). 62 − 48 = 14. Other choices give bigger differences, like 46 − 28 = 18 or 82 − 64 = 18.

questions.prompt: Owen is 4 years older than his sister Lily. In 3 years, their ages will add up to 30. How old is Owen now?
questions.hint: In 3 years, both of them get 3 years older. What do their ages add up to now?
questions.solution: In 3 years each is 3 years older, so the total grows by 6. Now their ages add up to 30 − 6 = 24. Take away Owen's extra 4: 24 − 4 = 20, and half is 10, so Lily is 10 and Owen is 14.

questions.prompt: At a Halloween party, each of the 6 kids gives one piece of candy to every other kid at the party. How many pieces of candy are given out in all?
questions.hint: How many pieces does one kid give away?
questions.solution: Each kid gives a piece to the 5 other kids, so each gives 5 pieces. 6 kids × 5 pieces = 30 pieces. (This is not like handshakes: Ana giving to Ben and Ben giving to Ana are 2 different pieces.)
